answer: Cross-community attestation diversity resists sybils: eligibility needs endorsements from K graders in DISTINCT seed-reachable communities partitioned from the trust graph. A ring is one dense cluster — a single thread — so however many keys it mints, its vouches all originate in one community and fill at most one diversity slot. Honest agents sit across the wider horizon of independent clusters and collect endorsements spanning many. A beacon of a thousand confined sybils cannot forge cross-community spread without paying the scarce cost of edges into other honest clusters.
